ops.title: The payload fetch buffers ranges in memory and never signals its children
ops.body:
The guest fetch script (internal/images/host.go, fetchScript) downloads 32 MiB ranges, eight in flight, each through curl | dd bs=<range> iflag=fullblock | cat > FIFO, and a consumer reads the FIFOs in order into tee and openssl.

Why memory and not files: Sprites have only 64 MB tmpfs mounts (/dev/shm, /run), and part files under /tmp (a disk) made the fetch 23.67 s against 12.70-13.19 s with dd buffers, on a 2.13 GB payload where one stream took 33.85-79.09 s. Dirty-page throttling couples file-backed parts to disk speed.

Why no kill on failure: stored $! values of finished jobs can be recycled by the kernel once bash reaps them, and the script runs as root during a create that spawns many processes. After a failed range the script drains the in-flight FIFOs to /dev/null and waits. Unblocking the FIFO is required anyway, because a writer blocked in open() would otherwise outlive the script and hold its stderr.

Why process substitution for --config: a here-string becomes a temp file on bash before 5.1 or for long strings; <(printf ...) is always a pipe, so the presigned URL never reaches a file.

wait $! on a background pipeline returns the pipefail status of the whole job, checked on bash 5.3.
